2027-04-16.title: Friday after the Second Sunday after Qyomtho
readings: The mediator of a new covenant; the blood of the covenant
Take the lowest place; invite the poor
2027-04-16.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Second Sunday after the Resurrection. On Fridays the Church remembers the Lord's Passion; in Qyomtho she remembers it in the light of the empty tomb.
2027-04-16.verse: For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance.
theo: Christ is risen! On this Friday of the Easter season the Letter to the Hebrews speaks of the Lord's death, but as something that has already borne its fruit. Jesus “is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance.” The Letter plays on a word that in Greek means both “covenant” and “will.” A will takes effect only when the one who made it has died; until then the heirs receive nothing. So with us: by his death on the Cross, Christ made the inheritance ours. Then the Letter recalls Mount Sinai, where Moses took the blood of the sacrifice, sprinkled the book and the people, and said, “This is the blood of the covenant that God has ordained for you.” In the Upper Room Jesus took the cup and used those very words of himself: “this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins” (Matthew 26:28). And here is the wonder of Easter: in every other will the one who makes it stays dead. Our testator rose on the third day, and he himself now hands the inheritance to his heirs.

The Gospel takes us to a meal. Jesus is a guest in the house of a leader of the Pharisees, and he notices “how the guests chose the places of honor.” He tells them: “When you are invited... go and sit down at the lowest place, so that when your host comes, he may say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’” This is more than good manners. It describes the way of Jesus himself, who “humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death” (Philippians 2:8), and whom the Father raised and exalted. “For all who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.” Then Jesus turns to his host: do not invite only those who can invite you back, but “invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind. And you will be blessed, because they cannot repay you, for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.” St John Chrysostom urged the families of Antioch to keep a room in their homes for Christ, that is, for the poor stranger, and to set a place for him at their table (in substance).

Notice the Easter word at the end of the Gospel: “the resurrection of the righteous.” Because Christ is risen, a kindness that is never returned on earth is not lost. It is stored up with God. Our Kerala celebrations know the struggle Jesus describes: the seating at a wedding, the chairs kept for important guests, the gift lists, the invitations sent with an eye to who will invite us back. This week, turn one of these customs around. Invite someone to your table who cannot repay you; give a gift that will not be recorded; at a function, take the lower chair gladly. And remember that at the Holy Qurbono every one of us is a guest who has been called up higher. We come not because we have earned the place, but because the host has said, “Friend, come.” The blood of the new covenant is given to sinners, and the inheritance is offered to all who are called.
outline: Ask: where do I sit when I am invited, and whom do I invite?
Point 1 · The blood of the new covenant
A will that the testator himself rose to carry out.
The way of Jesus, humbled and exalted.
Generosity that waits for God's reward.
“You will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
live: At the next function or meeting you attend, choose a lower seat gladly and serve someone else first.
This week, share a meal or a packet of food with someone who has no way of returning it.
2027-04-16.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, mediator of the new covenant, by your death you made us heirs of the eternal inheritance, and by your Resurrection you live to give it to us. Teach us your humility, that we may take the lowest place without bitterness and rejoice when others are honoured. Open our hands and our homes to the poor, the sick and the lonely, who cannot repay us, and keep our hope fixed on the resurrection of the righteous. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the Blood of the new covenant, poured out once on the Cross, is truly given to us for the forgiveness of sins, and the risen Lord calls each of us, unworthy guests, to come up higher to his table.

quick: Christ is the mediator of a new covenant, sealed in his Blood; risen, he himself gives us the inheritance.
Jesus teaches us to take the lowest place, as he did.
Kindness to those who cannot repay is rewarded at the resurrection of the righteous.
2027-04-16.action: Do one kind thing today for someone who cannot repay you.
2027-04-16.question: When I give, am I hoping to be repaid by people, or by God?

family.explain: Jesus was at a big dinner. He saw people rushing to sit in the best seats. He told them: sit in the last seat, and let the host call you up. Then he told the man who gave the dinner: next time, invite poor people, sick people and people who cannot walk or see, who cannot invite you back. God himself will reward you.
family.intention: We pray for families who do not have enough to eat today.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom could our family invite or help this month who cannot pay us back?”

illus: A father in Pathanamthitta district was planning his daughter's wedding. The list of guests was long and carefully arranged, and the first sitting of the wedding feast was reserved, as usual, for the important families. A week before the wedding his daughter asked him for one change: that the first sitting be given to the residents of a care home near their parish and to the workers who had built their house. Some relatives were unhappy. On the wedding day the old people were brought in first, and the workers came in clean shirts with their wives. The bride went from table to table serving payasam. Years later, of all the photographs from that day, that is the one the family keeps in the front room.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you invite us to your table though we are unworthy. Make us humble and generous like you. Amen.
share: He is the mediator of a new covenant (Hebrews 9:15). What has Jesus' death and Resurrection given me that I could never have earned?
Go and sit down at the lowest place (Luke 14:10). Where do I seek the place of honour?
Invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind (Luke 14:13). Whom does our group overlook?
pm.resp: Lord, make us humble and generous.
interc: For the Church, that she may always keep the first place at her table for the poor.
For those who are proud of their place and status, that they may learn the way of Jesus.
For the poor, the disabled and the lonely in our parish, that they may be welcomed and honoured.
For families preparing weddings and celebrations, that they may remember those who cannot repay.
For our departed, that they may receive the inheritance promised to those who are called.
pm.close: Father, by the Blood of the new covenant your Son made us your heirs, and by his Resurrection he lives to give us the inheritance. Teach us to take the lowest place and to open our tables to the poor, until we sit with all your saints at the resurrection of the righteous. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! The Letter to the Hebrews says that Jesus is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance (Hebrews 9:15).

A will takes effect only after death. Christ died, and his will is in force: forgiveness, adoption, eternal life. But this testator rose again on the third day. He himself gives us what he left us, especially his own Body and Blood in the Holy Qurbono.

In the Gospel Jesus watches the guests choosing the best seats, and he says: go and sit down at the lowest place (Luke 14:10). That is his own way. He took the lowest place on the Cross, and the Father raised him up. Then he tells the host to invite the poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind, because they cannot repay, and you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous (Luke 14:14).
Because Christ is risen, no unreturned kindness is wasted. This week let us take a lower seat gladly, and invite to our table someone who cannot invite us back. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus once saw people pushing to get the best chairs at a party. He said: go and sit in the last chair, and the host will call you up! He also said: when you have a party, invite people who are poor or sick, who cannot invite you back. God will reward you. Can you share something today with someone who cannot give you anything in return?

intro: Theme: “You will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
On this Easter Friday: the blood of the new covenant, the lowest place, and the generosity that waits for the resurrection.

points.h: The blood of the new covenant
sub: A covenant that is also a will.
Sinai's blood and the cup of the Upper Room.
The testator rose to give the inheritance himself.
q: Moses took the blood and dashed it on the people, and said, “See the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made with you in accordance with all these words.”
For this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
points.apply: Before receiving Holy Communion this week, thank the Lord in silence for one gift of his covenant.

sub: The way of the humbled and exalted Lord.
q: Do not put yourself forward in the king's presence or stand in the place of the great; for it is better to be told, “Come up here,” than to be put lower in the presence of a noble.
He humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death
points.apply: At your next gathering, choose the lower seat gladly and serve others first.

sub: Not only friends and rich neighbours.
The poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind.
q: Since there will never cease to be some in need on the earth, I therefore command you, “Open your hand to the poor and needy neighbor in your land.”
Has not God chosen the poor in the world to be rich in faith and to be heirs of the kingdom that he has promised to those who love him?
points.apply: Share a meal this week with someone who cannot repay you.

concl: By his Blood Christ made us heirs, and by his Resurrection he gives us the inheritance.
Those who take the lowest place and open their tables to the poor will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.
2027-04-16.resolve: This week, give one gift and one place of honour to someone who can never pay you back.
